questions.prompt: Castlebridge Logistics' legacy freight-rate lookup tool is an old desktop application with no modern connector. Which of the three capabilities under the "Power Automate" name, per Lesson 1, is built specifically to automate a screen like that one?
options: Desktop flows (RPA)
Cloud flows
Process mining
Power BI data alerts
questions.explain: Desktop flows are robotic process automation (RPA) — they click, type, and read data in older desktop applications that have no modern connector, exactly the freight-rate lookup tool scenario. Cloud flows connect apps through connectors; process mining analyzes existing system logs; Power BI data alerts aren't part of this three-way split at all.

questions.prompt: Match each trigger type or piece to what actually starts or happens in a flow, per Lesson 2.
right: Fires manually, such as a button tap in the Power Automate mobile app
A step the flow performs after the trigger fires; a flow can have many
Fires on an event in a connected service, like a new SharePoint item
Fires on a recurring schedule you define, like every morning at 6 AM
questions.explain: Automated triggers fire on an event in a connected service. Instant triggers fire manually, like a mobile-app button. Scheduled triggers run on a recurring schedule you define. An action is a step the flow performs after the trigger fires, and a flow can have many of them.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of Castlebridge's vacation-request approval flow, per Lesson 3's four-step overview, in the correct order.
items: When an item is created fires on the SharePoint vacation-request list
Start and wait for an approval sends the request and pauses the flow
A condition on the approver's response determines which branch runs
The matching branch sends a decision email built from dynamic content
The flow updates the original SharePoint list item with the final status
questions.explain: The flow starts with the SharePoint item-created trigger, then Start and wait for an approval pauses execution until someone responds. The response is then checked by a condition, which routes to the branch that emails the decision, and finally the original list item is updated — the same four-step shape (trigger, approval requested, decision emailed, list updated) shown in Lesson 3's overview diagram.

questions.prompt: Castlebridge wants an email to go out only when a shipment was approved AND its value exceeds $10,000, using the expression above. Why does this need to replace the simple three-box Condition instead of just adding to it?
options: The simple three-box Condition only builds one comparison at a time, so checking two things at once requires an expression using and()
Nothing needs to change — the three-box Condition can test two comparisons at once by adding a second row
It requires two separate Condition actions chained together, since and() isn't valid inside a Condition's value field
It requires a Switch action instead, since Condition can only compare text values, not numbers
questions.explain: The three-box condition (value, operator, comparison value) handles exactly one comparison. Checking more than one thing at once — approved and over $10,000 — means switching to an expression using and(), or(), or not() inside the condition's field, which is exactly what this expression does.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about Apply to each and Do until, per Lesson 5.
options: Apply to each requires an array to already exist before it can run
Do until checks its condition before each iteration runs, never after
Do until's inner actions always run at least once, because the check happens at the end of each pass
Apply to each has its own Count and Timeout settings that stop a runaway loop
Polling a shipment-tracking API until its status becomes Delivered, with no fixed list involved, fits Do until better than Apply to each
questions.explain: Apply to each needs an array that already exists to loop over. Do until checks its condition at the end of each pass, not the beginning, which is exactly why its inner actions always run at least once. Count and Timeout are Do until's own safety limits, not Apply to each's. Polling with no fixed list involved is the textbook Do until case.

questions.prompt: A maker tries to place an Initialize variable action inside an Apply to each loop in a Castlebridge flow, intending to reset a counter on every iteration. What actually happens, per Lesson 6?
options: The designer won't allow it — Initialize variable can only run at the flow's top level, never inside a loop, Condition, or Scope
It runs fine, and the variable resets to its starting value on every single iteration
It runs fine on the first iteration only, then is silently skipped on every iteration after that
It runs, but only Integer and Float variables are blocked from being initialized inside a loop
questions.explain: Initialize variable is restricted to the flow's top level — directly under the trigger or another top-level action — and can never be placed inside a Condition branch, an Apply to each loop, or a Scope. To change a variable's value inside a loop, you initialize it beforehand at the top level and use Set variable, which works anywhere, inside the loop instead.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: in the expression addDays(utcNow(), 7), the ________() function is evaluated first, since its result becomes an argument fed into addDays().
questions.explain: Functions nest inside each other, with the innermost one evaluated first. utcNow() runs first to get the current UTC date and time, and that result is then fed into addDays() along with 7 to produce a timestamp seven days from now.

questions.prompt: On the Office 365 Outlook trigger "When a new email arrives (V3)," which setting must be turned on for the actual file content of an incoming attachment — not just its name, size, and content type — to be available to the rest of the flow?
options: Include Attachments
Only with Attachments
Importance
Has Attachment
Get emails (V3)
Forward an email (V2)
questions.explain: Include Attachments is the trigger setting that passes through the actual file content of each attachment. Attachment metadata (name, size, content type) always comes through regardless, but the real file content only arrives once this setting is turned on.
questions.distractorExplain: Only with Attachments is a real trigger setting on the same connector, but it only filters which emails fire the trigger at all — restricting it to messages that have at least one attachment. It has no effect on whether that attachment's file content is actually passed through once the trigger fires; only Include Attachments controls the content itself.

questions.prompt: A Castlebridge dispatcher builds a flow that posts an adaptive card to the Dispatch Teams channel, but on first run nothing ever appears in the channel. Per Lesson 9, what is the single most common reason a Teams action silently fails like this?
options: The Workflows app isn't installed in the target Microsoft Teams
Adaptive cards require a premium Power Automate license that wasn't assigned
Post message in a chat or channel can't be combined with dynamic content
The flow's trigger type doesn't support any Teams actions
questions.explain: Before any Teams action in a flow will actually post anything, the Workflows app must be installed in the target Microsoft Teams, either from the Teams app store or by a tenant admin. This is called out as the single most common reason a Teams action in a new flow silently fails on its first run.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about the Excel Online (Business) connector's actions, per Lesson 10.
options: Every action requires selecting a formally defined Excel Table, not a plain cell range
If a key value matches more than one row, Update a row changes every matching row
List rows present in a table returns a maximum of 256 rows unless pagination is explicitly turned on
Filter Query supports more than one filter function per column for complex numeric comparisons
Filtering beyond what Filter Query supports is usually handled by piping List rows' results through a Filter array action
questions.explain: Every action needs a real Excel Table object, invisible to a plain range. If more than one row matches a key value, only the first match is affected, not every match. List rows caps out at 256 rows by default without pagination turned on, and Filter Query only allows one filter function per column — exactly why richer filtering, like a numeric comparison, gets pushed downstream into a Filter array action instead.

questions.prompt: Match each SharePoint term or action to what it actually is, per Lesson 11.
right: A SharePoint action that returns a filtered set of rows from a list
A SharePoint folder of actual files, like photos or PDFs
Structured SharePoint data with named columns, the same shape as a database table
The SharePoint action that adds a new document to a library
questions.explain: A list holds structured rows with named columns, the same shape as a database table. A library holds actual files. Get items returns a filtered set of rows from a list. Create file adds a new document to a library — lists and libraries are genuinely separate connector surfaces even though both can live on the same SharePoint site.

questions.prompt: Castlebridge wants a flow to email the ops team the moment a Power BI dataset refresh actually finishes, success or failure. Per Lesson 12, why can't this be built the same simple way as the dataflow-refresh case?
options: There's no dataset-refresh-completion trigger — Refresh a dataset only confirms the request was accepted, so the flow needs a delay plus a call to the Power BI REST API's refresh history to find the real result
Power BI datasets can't be refreshed from Power Automate at all, only dataflows can
When a dataflow refresh completes also covers datasets, so no extra work is actually needed
Dataset refresh notifications require a custom connector, since Power BI has no REST API for refresh history
questions.explain: Power Automate has a dedicated trigger for dataflow refresh completion, but no equivalent exists for datasets — the Refresh a dataset action only confirms the refresh request was accepted, not that it finished. Reliably notifying on a dataset refresh's actual result means adding a delay after calling refresh, then calling the Power BI REST API to pull the refresh history and branching on that status.

questions.prompt: Match each Castlebridge approval scenario to the correct Start and wait for an approval type, per Lesson 13.
left: A freight-damage claim over $5,000 needs both the operations manager and finance to sign off
A routine driver schedule swap just needs whoever sees it first to clear it
Approvers must respond one at a time, in a defined order, each gating the next
A maker-defined set of response options, where everyone named must still answer
right: Sequential approval
Approve/Reject – Everyone must approve
Custom Responses – Wait for all responses
Approve/Reject – First to respond
questions.explain: Everyone must approve requires every named approver to respond before the flow continues, exactly Castlebridge's over-$5,000 claim process. First to respond finishes on any single response, fitting a routine schedule swap. Sequential approval makes approvers respond one at a time, in order. Custom Responses – Wait for all responses uses maker-defined options but still requires every named approver to answer.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of Castlebridge's scope-based try/catch pattern around its Dataverse update step, per Lesson 14, in the correct order.
items: The main actions, including the Dataverse update, are grouped into a scope named Try
A second scope named Catch is added, with its Run After configured to trigger only when Try has failed
Inside Catch, the result() function pulls the full outcome of every action from the paired Try scope
A Filter array action narrows that output down to just the failed action's specific details
The narrowed error details are logged and included in a failure-notification email
questions.explain: The main work sits inside a Try scope, with a Catch scope whose Run After fires only on Try's failure. Inside Catch, result() returns every action's outcome from Try, Filter array narrows that down to just the failed action, and only then is that specific error logged and emailed — exactly the order Lesson 14 walks through.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a Recurrence trigger's Start time is always entered in ________, regardless of where the flow's owner is physically located.
questions.explain: Start time anchors the schedule to a specific date and time in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, always Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) — exactly why Castlebridge's Monday-morning flow converts the trigger's timestamp with convertFromUtc() before logging it for Eastern-time dispatchers to read.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: in the Dataverse model, a single shipment record in the Shipments table is one ________ — the same thing a spreadsheet would call one line, but with enforced data types and real security on top.
questions.explain: A row is one record inside a table — a single shipment is one row in the Shipments table. A column is one field on that record, and tables can relate to each other so a row can reference a row in another table instead of retyping data.

questions.prompt: Castlebridge wants a flow that reacts in real time any time a Shipments row is created, updated, or deleted, with no one manually clicking anything. Which Dataverse trigger type, per Lesson 17, fits?
options: When a row is added, modified, or deleted
When a row is selected
When an action is performed
List rows
questions.explain: When a row is added, modified, or deleted fires automatically whenever a chosen table changes, and the lesson calls it out as the one used for the large majority of Castlebridge's flows. When a row is selected requires someone to click the Flow button inside a model-driven app, and List rows isn't a trigger at all — it's an action.

questions.prompt: Castlebridge's finance team's SQL Server database is an on-premises install with no direct connection to the public internet. Per Lesson 18, what does a Power Automate flow need in place before it can reach that database at all?
options: An on-premises data gateway installed on a machine inside that network
A custom connector built specifically for that database
A Dataverse table mirroring the SQL Server schema
A DLP policy explicitly allowing SQL Server
questions.explain: An on-premises data gateway is required whenever the database isn't reachable from the public internet, which describes most corporate SQL Server installs. It's a small piece of software installed on a machine inside that network, letting a cloud-based flow reach a database it otherwise couldn't touch. A custom connector and a DLP policy solve different problems entirely.

questions.prompt: A flow's HTTP action calls Meridian TrackAPI and gets back a response. Select every true statement about reading that response, per Lesson 19.
options: A status code in the 200s means the call succeeded
A 401 means the request's URI or shipment ID was wrong
A 404 means the URI or shipment ID was wrong
A 500 means the problem is on Meridian's end, not the flow's
GET requests, like Meridian's tracking lookup, typically include a JSON body the same way a POST does
questions.explain: Codes in the 200s mean success. A 401 means the call wasn't authenticated correctly, not that the URI was wrong — that's what a 404 means. A 500 points to a problem on the API's own end. A GET request, like Meridian's tracking lookup, usually has no body at all; bodies are for POST and PUT.

questions.prompt: A maker wants to quickly test a tricky expression and reuse its result in five later steps, with no JSON parsing involved. Which action from Lesson 20 fits, and why?
options: Compose — it evaluates one expression and holds the result for reuse, with no parsing involved
Parse JSON — it's the general-purpose action for holding any expression's result
Parse JSON, because a schema is required before any expression can be reused later in a flow
Neither — expressions can only be reused by retyping them in every action that needs them
questions.explain: Compose is a scratchpad, not a parser — it evaluates one expression and holds the result so it can be inspected or fed into later steps, exactly how teams debug a tricky expression or build one reusable value instead of retyping it five times. Parse JSON does a genuinely different job: converting a JSON string into typed fields using a schema.

questions.prompt: Castlebridge needs a connection to its internal backend that keeps authenticating correctly even as individual employees come and go, with no human signing in interactively. Which identity and authentication flow, per Lesson 21, fits?
options: A service principal, authenticated with the OAuth client credentials grant
A user-delegated connection, authenticated with a specific employee's username and password
A user-delegated connection, automatically refreshed whenever the owning employee's password changes
A service principal, authenticated interactively through the same consent screen a person would see
A connection reference, which replaces the need for any authentication at all
An environment variable storing the employee's credentials as its value
questions.explain: A service principal is a non-human application identity registered in Microsoft Entra ID, authenticated with a client ID and secret (or certificate) rather than a username and password. It uses the OAuth client credentials grant — presenting its client ID and secret directly to Entra ID's token endpoint for an access token — with no human in the loop, exactly why it keeps working as employees come and go.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B describes a user-delegated connection, the opposite of what's needed here — it runs as a specific signed-in person and inherits exactly their access, so it breaks the moment that person leaves the company or changes their password. That fragility is precisely the problem a service principal exists to avoid.

questions.prompt: Put these sections of the custom connector wizard, per Lesson 22, in the order Castlebridge actually works through them.
items: General — the connector's icon, description, and base URL
Security — the authentication type the dispatch API expects, such as API Key
Definition — the actions and triggers, built from a real request and response using Import from sample
Code — optional custom C# to transform a request or response beyond the codeless definition
Test — a real connection is created and a real call is run before the connector is trusted in any flow
questions.explain: The wizard runs left to right through General, Security, Definition, an optional Code step, and finally Test — where Castlebridge actually calls its live dispatch API and confirms the response before trusting the connector inside any real flow.

questions.prompt: Castlebridge's child flow uses a SQL Server action, and when called from a parent flow it fails with an error saying it can't be used as a child workflow. Per Lesson 23, what is the most likely cause?
options: The child flow's SQL Server connection is still set to "Provided by run-only user" instead of "Use this connection" under Run only users settings
The child flow is missing a Respond to a Power App or flow action
The parent flow passed more inputs than the child flow's trigger defines
Child flows can never use any connector beyond built-in actions and Dataverse
questions.explain: Connections can't be passed from a parent flow to a child flow at run time. Any connection beyond built-in actions or Dataverse — like the SQL Server connection here — has to be set to "Use this connection" in the child flow's Run only users settings, embedding it directly. Leaving it as "Provided by run-only user" is exactly what produces this failure.

questions.prompt: Match each Solution-related term to what it actually is, per Lesson 24.
right: A tool that inspects a solution for problems before it's exported or deployed
Fully editable; used in development
A flow together with everything it depends on, like a custom connector or connection references
Locked down after import; used in test and production
questions.explain: An unmanaged solution is fully editable, the shape Castlebridge builds in dev. A managed solution is locked down after import, protecting test and production from casual edits. Solution Checker inspects a solution for problems before export or deployment. A Solution's whole purpose is bundling a flow with everything it depends on, like a custom connector, so the dependencies move together.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about environment variables and connection references, per Lesson 25.
options: An environment variable's definition — its data type and default value — travels inside the managed solution
An environment variable's current value is set per environment and is itself part of the managed solution
A connection reference lets the same flow authenticate as a different login in each environment without editing the flow
During import, Power Apps prompts for each environment variable's value for that target environment
Connection references exist specifically so an environment-specific server name can differ per environment
questions.explain: The definition (data type, default) travels inside the managed solution, but the current value is set per environment and is unmanaged, not part of the package. Connection references decouple which login a connector action uses per environment, and solution import does prompt for each environment variable's value for the target environment. Externalizing a differing server name is the environment variable's job, not the connection reference's — connection references are about which credential, not which value.

questions.prompt: Match each Power Platform environment type to what it actually is, per Lesson 26.
right: Expires after 30 days, one per user, good for a quick proof of concept
A non-production environment for development and testing, supporting copy and reset
Automatically created for every tenant, shared by every licensed user, with no backup guarantees
Intended for permanent, business-critical work, with real users and real data
questions.explain: Production is for permanent, business-critical work with real data. Sandbox is the non-production environment used for dev/test, supporting copy and reset operations. Default is auto-created per tenant with no backup guarantees. Trial expires after 30 days, one per user, suited only to a quick proof of concept.

questions.prompt: Castlebridge's DLP policy places SQL Server in the Business group and leaves Twitter in the default Non-Business group. Per Lesson 27's core rule, what happens to a flow that tries to read from SQL Server and post the result to Twitter?
options: It can't be saved — a single flow can never combine connectors from two different DLP groups
It saves and runs fine, since only Blocked connectors are actually restricted
It saves, but the SQL Server action silently returns no data at run time
It's allowed only if an administrator specifically approves that one flow
questions.explain: The entire DLP mechanism comes down to one rule: a single flow can't combine connectors from two different groups. SQL Server in Business and Twitter in Non-Business are different groups, so a flow combining them can't be saved at all — the maker isn't warned after the fact, the save itself is blocked, and an existing compliant flow would be suspended if a later policy change made it non-compliant.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Castlebridge's IT admin governs every flow tenant-wide from the Power Platform Admin Center, reached at admin.________.microsoft.com, not make.powerautomate.com.
questions.explain: Makers build flows at make.powerautomate.com; admins govern all of them tenant-wide from admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com — two different doors into two different experiences.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of promoting Castlebridge's "Shipment Exception Alerts" flow through its pipeline, per Lesson 29, in the correct order.
items: The flow is built and packaged inside an unmanaged solution in the Development environment
A maker clicks Deploy, and the pipeline exports the solution automatically
The pipeline validates the exported solution against the Test environment
The solution is imported into Test as a managed solution, with connections and environment variables already configured for that stage
After validation in Test, the same promotion repeats into Production
questions.explain: Development holds the editable unmanaged solution. Clicking Deploy kicks off the pipeline's automatic export, validation against the target, and import as a managed solution with that stage's own connections and variables already wired in — then, once Test has passed, the identical promotion repeats into Production.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about diagnosing a failed flow run, per Lesson 30.
options: Run history is retained for 28 days by default
An error containing "Unauthorized" or a 401/403 code usually means a connection expired or was never authorized
An error containing "Bad request" or "Not found" (400/404) usually points to an expired connection needing reauthorization
A 500 or 502 code usually means something is permanently broken inside the flow's own configuration
Resubmit re-runs a specific failed run immediately, using its original trigger data, without waiting for the next scheduled trigger
questions.explain: Run history keeps 28 days by default. Unauthorized/401/403 errors point to an expired or unauthorized connection, fixed by reauthorizing it. Bad request/Not found (400/404) errors instead point to a wrong setting inside an action, not a connection problem. 500/502 codes usually mean a temporary hiccup in the called service, not a permanent break in the flow's own configuration. Resubmit re-runs the specific failed run immediately with its original trigger data.
